questions.q: A large block of wood of mass $M = 5 . 99kg$ is hanging from two long massless cords. A bullet of mass $m = 10g$ is fired into the block and gets embedded in it. The (block $+$~bullet) then swing upwards, their center of mass rising a vertical distance $h = 9 . 8cm$ before the (block $+$ bullet) pendulum comes momentarily to rest at the end of its arc. The speed of the bullet just before the collision is:~(Take $g = 9 . 8{ms}^{- 2}$)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: Center of Mass, Momentum and Collision
questions.solution:
From energy conservation,

[after bullet gets embedded till the system comes momentarily at rest]

\left(M + m\right)gh = \dfrac{1}{2}\left(M + m\right){v}_{1}^{2}$
[${v}_{1}$ is velocity after collision]~

$∴ {v}_{1} = \sqrt{2\sigmah}$

Applying momentum conservation, (just before and just after collision)

$mv = \left(M + m\right){v}_{1}$

$v = \left(\dfrac{M + m}{m}\right){v}_{1} = \dfrac{6}{10 \times {10}^{- 3}} \times \sqrt{2 \times 9 . 8 \times 9 . 8 \times {10}^{- 2}}$

$\approx 831 . 55ms^{- 1}$

$

questions.q: Two bodies of mass $1$ kg and $3$ kg have position vectors $\overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}$ and $- 3\overset{^}{i} - 2\overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}$ respectively. The magnitude of position vector of centre of mass of this system will be similar to the magnitude of vector :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: Center of Mass, Momentum and Collision
questions.solution:
As we know, centre of mass is given by,& $\overset{→}{r}com = \dfrac{∑ {m}_{i}\overset{→}{r}i}{∑ {m}_{i}}$

$\overset{→}{r}com = \dfrac{m\left(\overset{^}{ı} + 2\overset{^}{ȷ} + \overset{^}{k}\right) + 3m\left(- 3\overset{^}{ı} - 2\overset{^}{ȷ} + \overset{^}{k}\right)}{m + 3m}$

$\overset{→}{r}com = \dfrac{- 8m\overset{^}{ı} - 4m\overset{^}{ȷ} + 4m\overset{^}{k}}{4m} = - 2\overset{^}{ı} - \overset{^}{ȷ} + \overset{^}{k}$

The magnitude of the position vector of the centre of mass is~$\sqrt{{2}^{2} + {1}^{1} + {1}^{2}} = \sqrt{6}$.

It is similar to the magnitude of the option A.

questions.q: A spherical body of mass $100g$ is dropped from a height of $10m$ from the ground. After hitting the ground, the body rebounds to a height of $5m$. The impulse of force imparted by the ground to the body is given by: (given $g = 9 . 8ms^{- 2}$)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: Center of Mass, Momentum and Collision
questions.solution:
Using equation of motion with constant acceleration, we can write:

${v}_{1} = \sqrt{2g{h}_{1}}$ and ${v}_{2} = \sqrt{2g{h}_{2}}$

Now, required impulse

$\overset{→}{I} = \Delta\overset{→}{p} = \overset{→}{p}f - \overset{→}{p}i$

Given, $M = 0 . 1kg$

Therefore,

$I = \Deltap = 0 . 1 ( \sqrt{2 \times 9 . 8 \times 5} - ( - \sqrt{2 \times 9 . 8 \times 10} ) )$

$= 0 . 1 ( 7\sqrt{2} + 14 ) \approx 2 . 39kgms^{- 1}$

questions.q: A particle of mass& $m$~with an initial velocity~$u\overset{^}{i}$~collides perfectly elastically with a mass~$3m$~at rest. It moves with a velocity~$v\overset{^}{j}$~after collision, then,~$v$& is given by&
questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: Center of Mass, Momentum and Collision
questions.solution:
From momentum conservation

$mu\overset{^}{i} + 0 = mv\overset{^}{j} + 3m\overset{→}{v} '$

$\overset{→}{v} ' = \dfrac{u}{3}\overset{^}{i} - \dfrac{v}{3}\overset{^}{j}$

From kinetic energy conservation~$\dfrac{1}{2}mu^{2} = \dfrac{1}{2}mv^{2} + \dfrac{1}{2} ( 3m ) \left(\left(\dfrac{u}{3}\right)$2 + $\left(\dfrac{v}{3}\right)$2)$

solving~$v = \dfrac{u}{2}$

$

Applying momentum conservation, we get

$3\left[\left(20 \times {10}^{- 3}\right) \times 100\right] = 10v$

$⇒ v = 0 . 6ms^{- 1}$

questions.q: The center of mass of a thin rectangular plate (fig - x ) with sides of length $a$ and $b$, whose mass per unit area $(\sigma)$ varies as $\sigma=\frac{\sigma_0 x}{a b}$ (where $\sigma_0$ is a constant), would be $\qquad$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: Center of Mass, Momentum and Collision
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} & d m=\sigma d A \\ & $\begin{aligned} d & =\sigma(d x)(d y)=\frac{\sigma_0 x}{a b}(d x)(d y) \\ x_{c o m} & =\frac{\int x d m}{\int d m}=\frac{\int x \frac{\left(\sigma_0 x\right)}{a b}(d x)(d y)}{\int_0 \frac{\sigma_0}{a b}(d x)(d y)} \\ & =\frac{\int_0^a x^2 d x \int_0^b d y}{\int_0^b x d x \int_0^b d y}=\frac{2 a}{3} \\ y_{c o m} & =\frac{\int y d m}{\int d m}=\frac{\int y\left(\frac{\sigma_0 x}{a b}\right)(d x)(d y)}{\int \frac{\sigma_0 x}{a b}(d x)(d y)}\end{aligned}$\end{aligned}=\frac{\int_0^a x d x \int_0^b y d y}{\int_0^a x d x \int_0^b d y}=\frac{b}{2}$
i.e., $\$vec{r}_{\mathrm{com}} \equiv  \left(\frac{2 a}{3}, \frac{b}{2}\right)$$

questions.q: A bullet of $10g$ leaves the barrel of gun with a velocity of $600ms^{- 1}$. If the barrel of gun is $50$ cm long and mass of gun is $3kg,$ then value of impulse supplied to the gun will be:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: Center of Mass, Momentum and Collision
questions.solution:
The formula to calculate the impulse& \left(J\right)$ on the gun is given by

$J = m \left(v - u\right) . . . \left($1\right)$

where,~$m$~is the mass,~$u$~is the initial velocity and~$v$~is the final velocity of the bullet.

Substitute the values of the known parameters into equation (1) to calculate the required impulse.

$\begin{cases}J \text{ and } = \text{ and } 10g \times \dfrac{1kg}{1000g} \times \left(600 - 0\right)ms^{- 1} \\ \text{ and } = \text{ and } 6Ns\end{cases}$

questions.q: Two particles of equal mass $m$ have respective initial velocities $u\overset{^}{i}$ and $u \left(\dfrac{\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j}}{2}\right) .$They collide completely inelastically. The energy lost in the process is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: Center of Mass, Momentum and Collision
questions.solution:
Conserving momentum
$mu\overset{^}{i} + m\left(\dfrac{u}{2}\overset{^}{i} + \dfrac{u}{2}\overset{^}{j}\right) = 2m \left({u}_{1}\overset{^}{i} + {u}_{2}\overset{^}{j}\right)
On solving
${u}_{1} = $\dfrac{3u}{4} and ${u}_{2} = $\dfrac{u}{4}
Change in K.E.
\left[\dfrac{1}{2}$mu^{2} + $\dfrac{1}{2}$m{ \left(\dfrac{u}{2}\sqrt{2}\right)}^{2}\right] - \left[\dfrac{1}{2}\left($2m\right)\left(\dfrac{9u^{2}}{16} + \dfrac{u^{2}}{16}\right)\right]$
$= \dfrac{3mu^{2}}{4} - \dfrac{5mu^{2}}{8} = \dfrac{mu^{2}}{8}$

questions.q: When kinetic energy of a body becomes 36 times of its original value, the percentage increase in the momentum of the body will be:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: Center of Mass, Momentum and Collision
questions.solution:
Kinetic energy $(K)=\frac{P^2}{2 m}\Rightarrow \mathrm{P}=\sqrt{2 \mathrm{mK}}$
If $K_f=36 K_i$ So, $\mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{f}}=6 \mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{i}}$\begin{aligned} \% \text { increase in momentum } & =\frac{\mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{f}}-\mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{i}}}{\mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{i}}} \times 100 \% \\ & =\frac{6 \mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{i}}-\mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{i}}}{\mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{i}}} \times 100 \% \\ & =500 \% \end{aligned}$$

questions.q:
In two different experiments, an object of mass $5$ kg moving with a speed of $25\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm{ms}^{-1}$ hits two different walls and comes to rest within
(i) $3$ second, (ii) $5$ seconds, respectively.
Choose the correct option out of the following :
options: Impulse and average force acting on the object will be same for both the cases.
Impulse will be same for both the cases but the average force will be different.
Average force will be same for both the cases but the impulse will be different.
Average force and impulse will be different for both the cases.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: Center of Mass, Momentum and Collision
questions.solution:
Impulse =~Change in momentum

$I = \Delta P$

Therefore, in both the cases the impulse is same.

Average force is defined as,

${F}_{avg} = \dfrac{\Delta P}{\Deltat}$

Since the time in the two cases is different, the average force will be different.

questions.q: A body of mass $1000$ kg is moving horizontally with a velocity $6ms^{- 1}$. If $200$ kg extra mass is added, the final velocity (in $ms^{- 1}$) is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: Center of Mass, Momentum and Collision
questions.solution:
From the conservation of linear momentum, it can be written that

$Mu = \left(M + m\right)v . . . \left($1\right)$

where, $M$ is the initial mass, $u$ is the initial velocity, $m$ is the extra mass added and $v$ is the final velocity of the composition.

From equation (1), it follows that

$1000 \times6 = 1200 \timesv ⇒ v = 5ms^{- 1}$

$

questions.q: Three objects $A, B$ and $C$ are kept in a straight line on a frictionless horizontal surface. The masses of~$A, B$ and $C$ are $m, 2m$ and $2m$ respectively. $A$ moves towards $B$ with a speed of $9ms^{- 1}$ and makes an elastic collision with it. Thereafter $B$ makes a completely inelastic collision with $C .$ All motions occur along the same straight line. The final speed of $C$ is :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: Center of Mass, Momentum and Collision
questions.solution:
Collision between $A$ and $B$

$m \times 9 = m{v}_{1} + 2m{v}_{2}$ (from momentum conservation)
$e = 1 = \dfrac{{v}_{2} - {v}_{1}}{9}$
$⇒ {v}_{2} = 6m\sec^{- 1}, {v}_{1} = - 3m\sec^{- 1}$
Collision between $B$~and $C$

$2m \times 6 = 4mv$ (from momentum conservation)
$v = 3ms^{- 1}$

questions.q: If ${10}^{22}$ gas molecules each of mass ${10}^{- 26}$ kg collides with a surface (perpendicular to it) elastically per second over an area $1m^{2}$ with a speed ${10}^{4}m / s,$ the pressure exerted by the gas molecules will be of the order of:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: Center of Mass, Momentum and Collision
questions.solution:
Total momentum transferred in one second $= n\left(2mv\right) = {10}^{22}\left(2 \times {10}^{- 26} \times {10}^{4}\right) = 2$
Force experienced by surface $= 2N$
Pressure on surface $= \dfrac{Force}{Area} = \dfrac{2}{1} = 2Pa$

questions.q: A rod of length $l$ has non-uniform linear mass density given by $ρ\left(x\right) = a + b\left(\dfrac{x}{l}\right)2,$ where $a$ and $b$ are constants and $0 \le x \le l$ The value of $x$ for the centre of mass of the rod is at:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: Center of Mass, Momentum and Collision
questions.solution:
$
${X}_{cm} = \dfrac{1}{M}\mathop{∫}_{0}^{ι}x . dM$
$dM = ρ . dx = \left(a + b\left(\dfrac{x}{ı}\right)2\right) . dx$
${x}_{cm} = \dfrac{∫ xdM}{∫ dm} = \dfrac{∫ xρdx}{∫ ρdx} = \dfrac{\mathop{∫}_{0}^{ι}x\left(a + \dfrac{bx^{2}}{ι2}\right)dx}{\mathop{∫}_{0}^{ι}\left(a + \dfrac{bx^{2}}{ι2}\right)dx}$
$= \dfrac{a{\left(\dfrac{x^{2}}{2}\right)}_{0}^{ι} + \dfrac{b}{{ι}^{2}}{\left(\dfrac{x^{4}}{4}\right)}_{0}^{ι}}{a{\left(x\right)}_{0}^{ι} + \dfrac{b}{{ι}^{2}}{\left(\dfrac{x^{3}}{3}\right)}_{0}^{ι}}$
$= \dfrac{a\dfrac{{ι}^{2}}{2} + b\dfrac{{ι}^{2}}{4}}{aι + \dfrac{bι}{3}} = \dfrac{\left(2a + b\right)}{ \left($3a + b\right)}\dfrac{ι}{4} \times3$
$= \dfrac{3ι}{4}\left(\dfrac{2a + b}{3a + b}\right)$

questions.q: A ball of mass $200g$~rests on a vertical post of height $20m$. A bullet of mass $10g$, travelling in horizontal direction, hits the centre of the ball. After collision both travels independently. The ball hits the ground at a distance $30m$ and the bullet at a distance of $120m$ from the foot of the post. The value of initial velocity of the bullet will be (if $g = 10ms^{- 2}$) :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: Center of Mass, Momentum and Collision
questions.solution:
Let initial velocity of bullet be $u$.

Given, mass of bullet~$m = 10g$~and mass of ball~$M = 200g$,

Initially ball is at height $5m$~and~at rest, the only acceleration acting is due to gravity.

Time of flight of each ball and bullet is~$t = \sqrt{\dfrac{2h}{g}}$.

Now, velocity of ball and bullet as~${v}_{1} = \dfrac{30}{\dfrac{2h}{g}}and{v}_{2} = \dfrac{120}{\dfrac{2h}{g}}$

As the collision is elastic, so applying conservation of linear momentum.

$mu + M\left(0\right) = M{v}_{1} + m{v}_{2}$

$⇒ \left(0 . 01\right)u = \left(0 . 2\right)\dfrac{30\sqrt{g}}{2h} + \left(0 . 01\right)\dfrac{120\sqrt{g}}{2h}$

$⇒ u = 300 + 60 = 360ms^{- 1}$

questions.chapter: Center of Mass, Momentum and Collision
questions.solution:
Using the law of& Momentum conservation

${m}_{1}{v}_{1} + {m}_{2} ( - {v}_{2} ) = 0$
$⇒ {m}_{1}{v}_{1} = {m}_{2}{v}_{2}$
$⇒ $\left(\dfrac{m1}{m2}) =\left(\dfrac{v2}{v1})$⇒ $\dfrac{\dfrac{4\piρr^{3}1}{3}}{4\piρr^{3}23} = \left(\dfrac{v2}{v1}\right)

It is given

~\dfrac{r1}{r2} = \dfrac{1}{2\dfrac{1}{3}}
$\text{and} \left(\dfrac{r1}{r2}\right)$3 = \left(\dfrac{v2}{v1}\right)\text{Therefore}, \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right) = \left(\dfrac{v2}{v1}\right)$
$⇒ \dfrac{v1}{v2} = \dfrac{2}{1}$

$

questions.q: A ball of mass $10$ kg moving with a velocity $10\sqrt{3}ms^{- 1}$ along the $x$ -axis, hits another ball of mass $20$ kg which is at rest. After the collision, first ball comes to rest while the second ball disintegrates into two equal pieces. One piece starts moving along $y$ -axis with a speed of $10ms^{- 1} .$~The second piece starts moving at an angle of $30 °$ with respect to the $x$ -axis. The velocity of the ball moving at $30 °$ with $x$ -axis is $xms^{- 1} .$~The configuration of pieces after the collision is shown in the figure below. The value of $x$& to the nearest integer is
questions.subject: Physics

Let the velocity of ${2}^{nd }$ fragment is $\overset{→}{v}$ then by conservation of linear momentum
$10 ( 10\sqrt{3} ) \overset{^}{i} = ( 10 ) ( 10\overset{^}{j} ) + 10\overset{→}{v}$
$⇒ \overset{→}{v} = 10\sqrt{3}\overset{^}{i} - 10\overset{^}{j}$

questions.q: Three identical spheres each of mass $M$ are placed at the corners of a right angled triangle with mutually perpendicular sides equal to $3m$~each. Taking point of intersection of mutually perpendicular sides as origin, the magnitude of position vector of centre of mass of the system will be $\sqrt{x}m$. The value of $x$ is
questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: Center of Mass, Momentum and Collision
questions.solution:
The diagram represents the locations of the masses as mentioned in the question.

For point& $1$,~$\overset{→}{r1} = 0\overset{^}{i} + 0\overset{^}{j}$~for point~$2$,~$\overset{→}{r2} = 3\overset{^}{i} + 0\overset{^}{j}$~and for point~$3$,~$\overset{→}{r3} = 0\overset{^}{i} + 3\overset{^}{j}$.

The formula for centre of mass is

$\overset{→}{r}com = \dfrac{{m}_{1}\overset{→}{r1} + {m}_{2}\overset{→}{r2} + {m}_{3}\overset{→}{r3}}{{m}_{1} + {m}_{2} + {m}_{3}}$

$⇒ \overset{→}{r}com = \dfrac{M\left(0\overset{^}{i} + 0\overset{^}{j}\right) + M\left(3\overset{^}{i}\right) + M\left(3\overset{^}{j}\right)}{3M}$

$⇒ \overset{→}{r}com = \overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j}$

\left|\overset{→}{r}com\right| = \sqrt{{1}^{2} + {1}^{2}} = \sqrt{2} = \sqrt{x}$

$⇒ x = 2$

$

questions.q: A uniform rod $AB$ of mass $2$ kg and Length $30$ cm at rest on a smooth horizontal surface. An impulse of force $0 . 2Ns$ is applied to end B. The time taken by the rod to turn through at right angles will be $\dfrac{π}{x}s,$ where $x =$ ____.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: Center of Mass, Momentum and Collision
questions.solution:
Impulse $J = 0 . 2Ns$

$⇒ J = ∫ Fdt = 0 . 2Ns$

Now, angular impulse $( \overset{→}{M} )$ will be

${M}_{c} = ∫ τdt$

$= ∫ F\dfrac{L}{2}dt$

$= \dfrac{L}{2} ∫ Fdt = \dfrac{L}{2} \times J$

$= \dfrac{0 . 3}{2} \times 0 . 2$

$= 0 . 03$

Moment of inertia of the rod about the centre of mass, ${I}_{cm} = \dfrac{ML^{2}}{12} = \dfrac{2 \times ( 0 . 3{)}^{2}}{12} = \dfrac{0 . 09}{6}$

Angular impulse will be equal to the change in angular momentum.

$M = {I}_{cm} \left({ω}_{f} - {ω}_{i}\right)$

$⇒ 0 . 03 = $\dfrac{0 . 09}{6} \left({ω}_{f}\right)$

$⇒ {ω}_{f} = 2rads^{- 1}$

For angular displacement, we can write \theta = \omegat

$⇒ t = $\dfrac{θ}{ω} = \dfrac{π}{2 \times 2} = \dfrac{π}{4}$s$.

Therefore, $x = 4$.

$
